newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Smuggling burns Nigerian Tobacco shares.
newsitem.headline: Smuggling burns Nigerian Tobacco shares.

text.p: Shares of Nigerian Tobacco Co (NTC) are going up in smoke because smuggling of imported brands has brought the company to its knees, dealers said on Friday.
The stock closed at 2.30 naira on Friday, 30 percent down from its opening price this year.
Traders said the company has a tough job dealing with smuggling but its officials said they are poised to win the battle against the menace.
"One of their major threats is entrenched smuggling interests," said Bayo Adeneji of securities trading house Hamilton Hammer.
NTC said this year that it planned to seek the assistance of government agencies to combat smuggling.
"Direct contact has already been made with the head of the customs services and the minister of agriculture," NTC chairman Olu Akinkugbe said in a statement.
The company subsequently embarked on a media campaign highlighting the danger smuggling poses to the tobacco industry.
But while it is still awaiting government's contribution to its efforts, dealers said NTC needs to do more to rebuild its fortunes.
"The company is not represented at the premium end of the cigarette market," one said, adding "They do not have any competing product in the market."
NTC's popular brands are only bought by smokers at the bottom end of the ladder, as most high fliers prefer imported brands, traders said.
Akinkugbe said agreements have been made with NTC's technical partner B.A.T Industries Plc of Britain in an effort to improve quality of its leading brand John Players Gold Leaf.
The British company holds a 60 percent majority in NTC.
A relocation of its factory to Zaria in the north from Ibadan in the southwest about two years ago also affected its fortunes because of transport costs, dealers said.
